title: Auth (OpenID Connect: authorize / token / revocation / MFA / discovery)
description: Standard OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.1 served by the identity service through the API gateway (ADR 0006, replacing the custom /v1/auth/login|refresh|logout of version 1.x). Clients are public (no secret) and use authorization code + PKCE S256; the mobile app signs in through the system browser (RFC 8252) and names its device with device_id. The access token is a 15-minute RS256 JWT with the same claims as 1.x; only the issuer changed, to a URL. Refresh tokens are opaque to clients, rotate on every use, and stop working when the session is revoked, the clinician deactivated or the device revoked. Request bodies of /connect/token and /connect/revocation are application/x-www-form-urlencoded; the definitions below describe their fields.

clients.description: Registered clients. admin-dashboard: browser, role admin only, audience melanin-wound-cdss-admin, refresh token 12 h, redirect <dashboard origin>/callback. mobile: the app on a registered device, audience melanin-wound-cdss-devices, refresh token 30 days, redirect lk.sliit.cdss:/oauth2redirect. The password grant exists only on mobile and only where Oidc:AllowPasswordGrant is on (device simulator and tests, never production).

authorizeRequest.description: Query of GET /connect/authorize. The identity service shows its login page (username and password, then the authenticator code when MFA is on), then redirects to redirect_uri with code and state. Errors before redirect_uri is verified are shown, never redirected.

redirect_uri.description: Must exactly match one registered for the client

scope.description: offline_access is needed for a refresh token

tokenRequest.description: Fields of POST /connect/token (form-encoded). A code is single use and lives 5 minutes. A refresh token is single use: each refresh returns the next one.

oneOf.description: Device simulator and tests only; refused unless Oidc:AllowPasswordGrant is on.

refresh_token.description: Opaque; present when offline_access was granted

id_token.description: Present when openid was granted; see idTokenClaims

error_description.description: For the password grant, the reason code: INVALID_CREDENTIALS, CREDENTIAL_LOCKED, MFA_REQUIRED, INVALID_TOTP, DEVICE_NOT_ALLOWED. For a refresh: INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN (expired, rotated, revoked, clinician deactivated or device revoked: sign in again). The device's offline queue is never affected by any auth error.

tokenError.description: HTTP 400 (401 for invalid_client). The API gateway may also answer 429 with Retry-After.

revocationRequest.description: Fields of POST /connect/revocation (form-encoded), used at sign-out. Revoking a refresh token ends its session. Always 200, even for an unknown token.

accessTokenClaims.description: Payload of the access JWT, signed RS256 by the identity service. Resource servers validate it locally with the keys from jwks. The Sync Gateway accepts only the device audience, so admin-dashboard tokens cannot push, pull or read patient records. oi_prst is OpenIddict's record of the presenting client.

idTokenClaims.description: Payload of the ID token, for display only (who is signed in). Never send it to an API.

mfaEnrollResponse.description: POST /v1/auth/mfa/enroll with an access token. The authenticator app shows the account as melanin-wound-cdss.

mfaConfirmRequest.description: POST /v1/auth/mfa/confirm with an access token; MFA is on once a first code is confirmed.

openidConfiguration.description: GET /.well-known/openid-configuration. The issuer is fixed; endpoint URLs follow the address the caller used (the API gateway for clients, the identity service inside Docker).

jwks.description: GET /.well-known/jwks (the jwks_uri). Public keys only; cache it and refetch when a token carries an unknown kid.
